title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: In Corollary 2(b), linearity is only demanded for λ ∈ A. That does not pin down C on degree-0 cocycles Λ = A·B^p, nor on Λ-multiples of the x^{p-1}dx. Uniqueness, and the computation in Corollary 3, need Frobenius-semilinearity over Λ: C(b^p ω) = b̃·C(ω). Grothendieck in effect uses this in Corollary 3 ('x^{-p} ∈ Λ') and in b'), so (b) as written is too weak for the claimed uniqueness.
The first expression in d), dx/x ⊗_B 1_A, is ill-typed (it should live over B̃). The second expression, dx̃/x̃ ⊗_{B̃} 1_Λ, is the correct one.
Small notational slips: 1_A should be 1_Λ, and a final 'Λ' is written where 1_Λ is meant.

ideas.what: Characterisation of the relative Cartier operation as the unique Frobenius-semilinear multiplicative map on closed forms that kills exact forms and sends x^{p-1}dx to dx̃
ideas.modern_name: Cartier operator / inverse Cartier isomorphism (relative version)
ideas.usually_credited_to: P. Cartier (1957); relative form in Katz, 'Nilpotent connections and the monodromy theorem' (1970), §7, and Deligne–Illusie (1987)
ideas.where_published: Standard via Katz IHES 39 (1970); not in EGA/SGA to my knowledge

ideas.what: Cartier operation on logarithmic forms: C(dx/x) = dx̃/x̃
ideas.modern_name: C fixes dlog forms (basis of the logarithmic de Rham–Witt / ν(r) sheaves)

ideas.what: Reduction to the absolute case when A → B lands in B^p (e.g. A perfect), with B reduced giving C: Z*(B) → Ω*_B and C(f^p ω) = f C(ω)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard exposition of the relative Cartier isomorphism, its uniqueness characterisation and its value on dlog forms. All of it is in Cartier, Katz (1970) and later standard references. The only noteworthy point is the minor gap in the stated linearity condition.
